[0] Last month we ran a poll, and the overwhelming majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should get out of the advertising business.

[1] Ads have now landed in Apple Maps in the US and Canada, and my take is that they are as bad as you'd expect…

[2] Apple first previewed in March that ads would begin appearing in its Maps app at some point this summer. We got our first look at them yesterday, and Apple has confirmed that the promotional campaign has rolled out over the past few days. All users in the US and Canada will see the ads over the next several weeks.

  • [3] Before search: Suggested Places in the search sheet will include ads.
  • [4] After search: Ads will appear in relevant positions in search results.

[5] Apple says that privacy is a key focus.

[6] I absolutely believe all of that, but I still think this is a very bad decision, for two reasons.

[7] First, while Apple does not deliver personalized ads via any form of tracking, nearly every other app and website does. Most people will assume this iPhone maker is doing the same thing — and regardless of how unfair that perception may be — it damages the company's reputation for protecting user privacy.

[8] Second, it's cheap. Ads are a necessary evil in the ecosystem of app and web publishing: it's ads that allow free apps and websites to operate. But Apple doesn't need ad revenue to operate: the company already charges premium prices for premium hardware. Ads simply don't fit the company's image.

[9] I believe it was John Gruber who compared ads in Apple apps to those annoying Intel Inside stickers on cheap Windows laptops. Of course, we understand that companies making cheap laptops need to pull out all the stops to find revenue streams, but we'd never expect Apple to cheapen the perception of its MacBooks by sticking them on. So why would we want to see ads inside the built-in apps on our Apple devices?

[10] I'm sticking firmly to my view that Apple has no business getting into advertising.
